author: Associated Press
description:
• Recruiting report prepared for Raiders’ 2024 search

  • Lawyers say assessment contains racial stereotypes

  • Flores sued NFL over discriminatory hiring in 2022

A recently unsealed recruiting report on Brian Flores contains multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach’s discrimination lawsuit against the NFL, according to his lawyers.

The Korn Ferry report, made public on Tuesday and obtained by the Associated Press, lists six strengths and seven weaknesses that Flores’ attorneys say demonstrate the league’s continued reliance on racial stereotypes in hiring and its retaliation against the coach for his lawsuit alleging racial discrimination.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Chip on his shoulder’: Brian Flores lawyers condemn racial stereotypes in NFL coaching report

author: Dara Kerr
description:
Researchers say ‘AI worms’ could soon infiltrate internet-connected devices amid calls for increased guardrails

Anthropic is warning that some of its artificial intelligence models could soon become “self-replicating” and find ways to infiltrate internet-connected devices, such as smart fridges and automatic vacuum cleaners.

Once this happens, the company said, the models could power themselves within these devices without the need of datacenters. Such self-replication would represent a major loss of control of a runaway AI model.

Continue reading...
title: AI in your oven? Anthropic warns models ‘months away’ from self-replication on smart devices

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Former QB fought with 69-year-old last October

  • Fox Sports parted ways with Sanchez over incident

  • Sanchez was charged over Indianapolis confrontation


Former NFL quarterback and Fox Sports analyst Mark Sanchez has reached an agreement in principle with the truck driver who stabbed him during an altercation last October, according to the Athletic.

Sanchez was stabbed and pepper sprayed by Perry Tole, who was 69 at the time, during the incident in Indianapolis, where the former New York Jets star was due to cover an NFL game between the Colts and Las Vegas Raiders. Prosecutors said Tole used pepper spray and a knife to de
title: Former NFL star Mark Sanchez reaches settlement over stabbing altercation

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Katie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hot

Well, that was weird. Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, made her debut on the podium on Tuesday with all the warmth, wisdom and political dexterity of an AI avatar.

Zacharia was all stilted delivery, nervous tics and lack of eye contact. With an eerie lack of emotion, she served up pro-Trump talking points, took only three questions and vanished after 14 minutes. It was like the West Wing had turned into uncanny valley.

Continue reading...
title: Enter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debut

author: Agencies
description:
• Game 3 moved up a day to avoid conflict

  • Dream to host at 17,000-seat State Farm Arena

  • Potential Game 6 venue remains uncertain

The WNBA has moved up Game 3 of the finals by a day so the Atlanta Dream can host the Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena. The league has also moved up the tipoff time for Game 4 of the best-of-seven series.

Game 3 will now take place on Wednesday 21 October. Game 4 will tip off at 1pm ET on Saturday 24 October, two and a half hours earlier than originally scheduled.

Continue reading...
title: WNBA moves finals schedule to allow Atlanta Dream to play at larger arena

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
James Robertson was the state’s 17th execution this year, amid scrutiny over failed lethal injection of Christa Pike

  • US plan to livestream execution elicits global condemnation

Florida put to death a convicted murderer in the state’s first execution since September’s botched attempt involving Christa Pike in Tennessee, on Tuesday.

Officials said James Robertson, 63, was pronounced dead after he received a three-shot series of lethal injections at a Florida state prison in Raiford.

Continue reading...
title: Florida carries out execution amid scrutiny over botched Tennessee attempt

description:

author: Jack Snape
description:
A handful of increasingly competitive teams are expected to at least provide intrigue in what is likely to be the best tournament the sport has witnessed

Critics will dismiss the men’s Rugby League World Cup as a provincial oddity, or a forgettable postscript to a long NRL season. Worse, they will question its legitimacy.

A “world” cup, they will taunt, pointing to participants hailing exclusively from the trans-Tasman coastlines and Pacific archipelagoes, with a sprinkling of northern Europe. And, oh yes, Lebanon – even if it is largely via Lakemba in western Sydney.

Continue reading...
title: Australian success is not guaranteed but who can stop the Rugby League World Cup hosts?

author: Lex McMenamin
description:
Author Natasha Lennard discusses how to disrupt the ‘certainties’ that don’t serve us and how to fight back

At the onset of the Covid pandemic in 2020, journalist Natasha Lennard started noticing a constant thrum of collective apprehension, epitomized in the phrase “in these uncertain times”. The expression acknowledged we didn’t have solutions for many of society’s problems: a globally spreading virus, the rise of the far right and stark “haves v have-nots” inequalities. In the years since, that “uncertainty” hasn’t gone anywhere, risking enabling paralysis – not knowing where to start to fix things and therefore giving up before trying.

In her new book, On Un/Certainty: The Uses of Doubt in Dangerous Times, Lennard, who also was an organizer in the 2
title: How to escape our collective paralysis in ‘these uncertain times’

author: Eduardo Porter
description:
The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for him

There is a manic quality to Donald Trump’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’s midterm elections to convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.

title: Is punishing the poor Trump’s last hand to play?

author: Jack Snape
description:
• Situation is being monitored by global players’ union Fifpro

  • Tournament is due to kick off in January with five venues in Riyadh

Asia’s elite men’s footballers are on edge as they prepare to travel to conflict-affected Saudi Arabia for January’s Asian Cup.

Multiple missile strikes by the Houthis on Riyadh’s international airport in recent days have killed more than a dozen people and wounded hundreds.

Continue reading...
title: Fresh concerns over 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia after missile strikes in Riyadh

author: Presented by Michael Safi with Julian Sancton; produced by Guy Szafman, Alex Atack and Ross Burns; executive producer Elizabeth Cassin
description:
Journalist Julian Sancton on the story of the most valuable shipwreck in history and who could end up with its treasures

A few years ago, the journalist Julian Sancton came across a story about a shipwreck found off the coast of Colombia. Onboard were treasures supposedly worth $1bn – which, he thought, must’ve been a typo. But it wasn’t. “It was supposedly billions, many tons, more than 100 tons of gold and silver,” he told Michael Safi.

He wrote a piece for Vanity Fair about the extraordinary 300-year mystery of where this ship had sunk, and how it had been finally found a decade ago. But the more Julian dug into the story, the more he realised that the tale of the man who had done more than anyone to find the San José was just as tantalising.

Continue reading...
title: The billion-dollar shipwreck and the man who tried to find it – podcast
